name: Joel Arendt
life: “I still remember packing lunches an hour before anyone else stirred.” On Tuesday, near Harbour Bakery, Joel buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I spent forty years packing those two lunches. My partner asked what retirement will change for me.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a charcoal zip cardigan and a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. Joel has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, with a thin scattering of white hair over the crown. Joel steadies a cup with both hands while listening during a conversation.
personality: Joel carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To give the retiring worker's partner a real voice about home life.
family: Ely Kern is Joel’s younger cousin. Joel chooses whether to use it. Ely saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *A tide at noon*, Ely says, “I sent guests down in polished shoes. One guest took hers off and stayed for hours.”
connections: Lionel Wu. Packed lunches and one last scorecard complicate the story that only two people are retiring.

reactions.situation: A younger worker is asked to perform the final lift
reactions.response: Joel lets the trainee carry out the job they are qualified for and keeps space for the retirees to watch.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Joel brings the envelope to the counter unopened and stays long enough to make a note of who accepted it.

reactions.situation: If a friend asks for a false alibi for an ordinary missed appointment
reactions.response: Joel offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
